title: Bring an existing project in
text: This page tells how to add the stack to a project that already has code, a Justfile or an AGENTS.md. Each step was run on 2026-11-19 with a new package cache. For a project that starts in an empty folder, read Start a Python, TypeScript or Rust project. The machine needs the same programs as for a new project. What the machine needs lists them.

title: Bring an existing project in
text: Term Meaning recipe A command in a Justfile. just NAME runs the recipe NAME. shared recipe A recipe that the installer writes, in .agents/install.just or in .agents/just/. the block The lines that the installer adds at the top of your Justfile. step One check of just check, such as lint or test.

title: Bring an existing project in
text: The project has no just install yet, so the first install runs from a clone of jnterfaces. Clone it into the folder of package clones: git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces" The installer clones each other package that it needs into the same folder.

title: Bring an existing project in
text: In the folder of the project, run the installer from the clone: uv run "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py" --profile python --target . Use --profile typescript or --profile rust for another language. At a terminal, the installer first asks which roles to install, then it asks the setup questions. With no terminal, for example when an agent runs it, the installer takes the default roles, tasker and prose. Then it prints the setup questions, writes nothing and stops: Key Question Answers issues Which Gest tasks become GitHub issues? top (the default), development or none integration Run the integration tests in just check, or only in just verify? check (the default) or verify tasker One branch in the main checkout, or a worktree for each task? Only with the tasker role. git (the default) or gitwt review-model Which model does the adversarial review? strongest (the default), or any model name docs-publish Publish the docs site of a public repository after a merge to main? Only with the docs role. yes (the default) or no The line then: of the questions gives the arguments to add, one --answer KEY=VALUE for each key. Add them to the uv run command, for example: uv run "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py" --profile python --target . \ --answer issues=none --answer integration=check --answer tasker=git --answer review-model=strongest --defaults takes the default roles and the default answer of each question.

title: Bring an existing project in
section: Step 3: read the block in your Justfile
text: Your Justfile stays yours. The installer adds one block at its top: # begin lines of jnterfaces, the installer, from jnterfaces at 361dcc3. # Last written to Justfile by `install_stack.py --profile python --target .`. The record is parts."Justfile" in .agents/stack.json. import? '.agents/install.just' export JLOG_RUN := env("JLOG_RUN", uuid()) # end lines of jnterfaces. They stay while the project keeps .agents/stack.json. The import? line reads the shared recipes. The JLOG_RUN line gives one run ID to each just call inside one just check, so that the run log of jlog keeps them together. The commit and the command in the comments change with each run. The installer leaves out a line that your Justfile already has. It adds no block to a Justfile that starts with a #! line or that is a symlink. How the stack fits together lists each case.

title: Bring an existing project in
section: Step 4: fix a clash of recipe names
text: Some names of the shared recipes clash with a recipe of yours. Others let your recipe take their place. The names that clash. .agents/install.just has the recipes install, uninstall and env-lab, and the variable jn_copier. When your Justfile has one of these names, just stops with this error: error: Recipe `install` first defined on line 7 is redefined on line 16 Then the installer takes its block out again, and it tells you to rename your recipe. Your own install recipe stays, so just install still runs your old recipe and not the installer. To fix it, rename your recipe, for example to setup. Then run the uv run command of step 2 again. The block stays this time. The name of a profile, such as python, also clashes. So does a recipe of a role that is on, such as review, worktree-new or ci-gate of the tasker role, or prose-check of the prose role. For these, the installer stops, writes nothing in .agents/just, and names the clash. The names that you can keep. .agents/just/index.just leaves out each name that your Justfile has, so your recipe takes its place. These names are the recipes of the profiles, such as setup, fmt, lint and test, the steps of just check that no role gives, and verify, check and ci. For example, your setup then takes the place of the setup of the profile, which runs uv sync. A recipe of yours with the name of a step must end with the line jlog step NAME, for example jlog step test. Without that line, jlog pass fails at the end of just check. A check of yours must end with the line jlog pass.

title: Bring an existing project in
section: Step 5: map your names in AGENTS.md
text: When the project already has an AGENTS.md, the installer adds only its own blocks to it. Keep the names of your recipes. Write the mapping from each concept to your recipe in AGENTS.md, for example “full local check: just check” or “install the packages: just setup”. The just skill tells an agent to use the names that AGENTS.md maps.

title: Bring an existing project in
text: The first commit goes through the commit gate of the tasker role. The gate needs a record of each agentic target that the change needs, and a pass of just check for the tree that you commit. It checks the whole worktree, with the files that are not staged too. Do the steps in this order: Stage the files, and run just check. Fix each step that fails. Run just review, and each other agentic target that the change needs. They and their fixes can change the files. Stage all the changes, and run just check again. Commit. git add --all just check When the gate stops, its message names what is missing. What to commit lists the files.

title: jnterfaces
text: jnterfaces is a package of agent skills for the command interface of a project. An agent skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that Codex, Claude and other agents read. The interface has three parts: The Justfile. Its recipes are the commands of the project. The packets of jagt. A packet is a block of text in a fixed format. A Just target emits one to hand a task to an agent, or to return a result. The file stages of cx. A stage is a recipe line that runs again only when its inputs, its outputs or its command change. The documentation site is https://rahuldave.github.io/jnterfaces/. It is built from docs/. just docs previews it, and just docs-publish publishes it to the branch gh-pages. Skill Use it when just You write, change or run a Justfile, or map workflow concepts to recipes. jagt-protocol A Just target emits an AGENT_TASK v1, AGENT_RESULT v1 or AGENT_TASK_DRAFT v1 packet. cx A recipe has expensive stages that read files and write files.

title: jnterfaces
text: jnterfaces is the base of every project. Besides Git, a project needs three programs only, just, uv and jlog. A profile can need more programs, such as rustup for Rust, and it names them in the key programs of its profile.json. One command installs everything else: just install just install comes from the file .agents/install.just, which jnterfaces installs in the project. The Justfile of the project imports that file. To start a new project, clone jnterfaces once and run its installer: git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces ~/.local/share/skill-packages/jnterfaces uv run ~/.local/share/skill-packages/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py --profile python Start a new project gives each step, from an empty folder to a project whose checks pass. For a project that already has code or a Justfile, Bring an existing project in gives each step, and tells how to fix a clash of recipe names. On the first install at a terminal, the installer asks which roles to install. It saves the answers in .agents/stack.json. If you name only roles, the installer asks nothing and turns on only the named roles. If you also name a profile or a tool, it turns on the default roles too. Without a terminal, a named profile takes the default roles. A later just install installs the same set again, so just install also updates a project. At a terminal, it asks only about a role that is newer than the saved set.

title: jnterfaces
text: A role names a job, and a package does that job. So the package behind a role can change and the name stays. The installer asks about each role. Press Enter to keep the default: Role What it installs Package Default cx the cx skill jnterfaces no jagt-protocol the jagt-protocol skill jnterfaces no docs the docs skill, a smalldocs site in docs/, docs-check in just check, and docs-publish with its CI workflow. The docs role tells more. jnterfaces no tasker the Gest g* skills, which track work agent_gest_git_skills yes prose the writing guide, its checker, the declaude skill, from the declauding skill by Oskar Austegard, and the writing flow: an instruction, two hooks and a GitHub workflow nossaifd yes reporter the lanes skill, which reports requests for human attention sklanes no The old names gest, nossaifd and sklanes still work for tasker, prose and reporter. Variants. A role can have variants, such as just install tasker=gitwt. The record saves the variant, so a later just install keeps it: Variant of tasker How the work goes git, the default on a branch in the main checkout gitwt each task in its own Git worktree, and the main checkout stays on main jj with jj. It is not ready yet, so the installer refuses it. The g* skills and the hooks of agent_gest_git_skills read the variant with just tasker-mode. In a project that jnterfaces started, the role also adds the worktree recipes just worktree-new NAME, just worktree-sync, just worktrees and just worktrees-prune. The recipes of a role. A role package can ship a recipe file, .agents/just/roles/ .just. In a project that jnterfaces started, the index imports it. For example, prose gives just prose-check, which checks the Markdown of the project. For another project, the installer names the line to add to its Justfile. The docs role. just install docs gives the project a docs site, for any language: It writes once docs/_smalldocs.yml, docs/index.md and the workflow .github/workflows/docs-publish.yml. It adds docs/_site/ to .gitignore. The theme is Atelier, with a light mode and a dark mode. The role writes the theme into docs/_extensions/atelier/, and the config sets theme: atelier. It adds two lines to .gitattributes, so that git diff --check accepts the line ends of the theme files and of their copy in the docs skill. just docs-check is a step of just check. It runs smalldocs check docs, then the api-check of each language that has one. just docs previews the site, and just docs-build builds it. just docs-publish publishes the site to the gh-pages branch, only when gh repo view says that the repository is public. It skips a private repository, and the answer docs-publish=no. When gh fails, it skips on your machine, and it fails in CI, so a missing token shows. The workflow runs just docs-publish after each push to main, with GH_TOKEN set. Once, you choose the branch gh-pages under Pages in the settings of the repository. just uninstall docs takes out the line and the recipes. Your pages stay. The workflow goes too, unless you changed it. Starter files. A role can write a starter file, such as the AGENTS.md of tasker, once, when the project has none. The starter is yours from then on. just uninstall takes out only the lines that the role added to it, and the file stays.

title: jnterfaces
text: Install git, just, uv and jlog. jlog logs each line of the recipes that just install writes. To install the release binary of jlog, run this line. It puts jlog in ~/.local/bin, so put that folder on PATH. curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rahuldave/jlog/v0.3.0/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --tag v0.3.0 To build jlog from source instead, clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jlog, run git checkout v0.3.0 in the clone, then run just install. Choose the folder of the package clones. The default is ~/.local/share/skill-packages. To use another folder, export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR in your shell profile first, for example export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR=~/Projects. just install in a project finds the clones in that folder only. Without the variable, it uses the default folder, also when you ran the first install from another clone. Clone jnterfaces into that folder: git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces" Make the project, and run the installer from the clone: mkdir app && cd app && git init uv run "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py" --profile python Use --profile typescript for TypeScript, or --profile rust for Rust. The installer clones the other packages that it needs, writes the starter Justfile, and adds the tools. Run just verify. A project with no code yet passes. A Rust project always has code, because cargo init writes src/main.rs. Its steps run with --locked, so first make Cargo.lock with just setup. The steps also check the docs, so add a //! doc line at the top of src/main.rs. On the first commit, coverage-check fails on each line that no test runs, and no test runs the main of cargo init. So write a test in tests/ that runs the binary, from env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_NAME"). For a library, run cargo init --lib --vcs none before the install. cargo init names the package after the folder, so a folder name that is not a valid crate name fails. Examples are a name that starts with a digit, a name with a . or a space, a Rust keyword such as fn, and test. For such a folder, run cargo init --vcs none --name NAME first. Put the code in the place that the profile expects: Profile Code Tests python Modules at the top of the project, such as app.py, or a package folder tests/test_NAME.py. pytest finds the modules at the top, because the test tool sets pythonpath. typescript src/, for example src/app.ts src/NAME.test.ts, which imports the code as ./app.js. rust src/, as cargo init makes it Unit tests in the module, and the files in tests/ Run just fmt to format the code, then just verify again. Commit the project, with .agents/, .claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/workflows/, the Justfile and the config files. .gitignore already leaves out what a command makes again, such as .venv/ or node_modules/. Later, just install --update gets the new commits of each package, and just install --check compares the record with the files. Start a Python, TypeScript or Rust project is the guide to a new project. It gives each tool, recipe, hook and config file, with examples. Bring an existing project in is the guide to a project that already has code or a Justfile.

title: jnterfaces
text: A tool is one unit of the setup of the project, such as lint. It brings its packages, its config files and its recipes. A profile, such as python, is a language. It sets the default roles and the tools. Each profile is a package of its own, and stack.json names it: Profile Package Tools Default tools The command that adds a tool python jnprofile-python lint, integration, test, docstring, api, typecheck lint, test, docstring, api uv add --group ... typescript jnprofile-typescript lint, typecheck, test, docstring all npm, which uvx runs from nodejs-wheel rust jnprofile-rust lint, typecheck, test, docstring, toml all but toml none: each tool uses programs, such as cargo-llvm-cov and taplo, which the key programs names On the first install, the installer finds the profile from the files of the project, such as pyproject.toml, or you name it with --profile. A project with both pyproject.toml and Cargo.toml, such as a Python package with a Rust extension, gets both profiles. After that, the installer uses the profiles of the saved record, also when the record has no profile. The recipes follow the tools. The profile package has one recipe file for each tool. just install writes a module for each profile in .agents/just, which imports the recipe files of the installed tools only. It also writes .agents/just/index.just, which .agents/install.just imports. Commit the files in .agents/just. .agents/install.just imports the index with import?, so just gives no error when the index is missing. A clone without the index does not have the recipes of the profiles and roles. So just install names each file there that git does not track, and just install --check fails when one of them is gone. In a project that jnterfaces started, with its starter Justfile: just python lint runs the lint of one language. just lint runs the lint of each language of the project. just verify runs every installed check of each language, then git diff --check. just check runs the steps of every project, from fmt-check to diff-check, and ends with jlog pass. A step that no profile, role or recipe of the Justfile has is a no-op step that logs the skip. So in a new project with no language, just check passes. just ci is what CI checks. It runs ci-gate, then the steps in the list ci of .agents/stack.json. A role with a commit gate gives ci-gate, which checks the trailer of the gate on each commit. ci-gate is a step of just check too, and each step in the list must be a step of just check. So CI checks only a part of just check. The list is empty at first. The steps of just check. just check runs these steps, in this order: tools-check release-check ci-gate fmt-check lint typecheck test integration coverage-check docstring-check docs-check prose-check diff-check The prose role gives prose-check, the tasker role (agent_gest_git_skills) gives release-check and ci-gate, and the installer gives tools-check and diff-check. An older tasker role whose ci-gate does not end with jlog step ci-gate stays out of just check, and the installer says to update it. tools-check checks that each program of .agents/stack.json is there, at its version floor. Each profile gives the steps of its installed tools: Profile Steps test-paths python lint, test, typecheck yes typescript fmt-check, lint, typecheck, test, coverage-check, docstring-check yes rust fmt-check, lint, typecheck, test, coverage-check, docstring-check yes coverage-check fails on each changed line of code that no test runs, and docstring-check fails on each item with no doc comment. test-paths is a recipe, not a step. It runs only the tests of some test files. The test-parent recipe of the tasker role runs it with the added and changed test files, on the parent commit. A recipe of the Justfile with the name of a combined recipe, such as lint, takes the place of the combined recipe. The index leaves that name out. A project with a Justfile of its own gets the same index. The installer adds a block of two lines to that Justfile. They are import? '.agents/install.just', and the line of the run ID, export JLOG_RUN := env("JLOG_RUN", uuid()). .agents/stack.json records the hash of each file that just install writes in .agents/just, and the installer changes only a file whose hash is the recorded one. With more than one language, a combined recipe gives the same arguments to each language. The source files. A profile can name the globs of its source files with the key code of profile.json, for example **/*.rs. just install copies them into the key code of .agents/stack.json, for each profile. The commit gate of agent_gest_git_skills reads them as @code. The other files. A shared file, such as .gitignore, is a file that you and the installer both add to. A profile, a tool or a role adds a part to each shared file that it needs, and takes out only its part. A part is one of three kinds: a block of lines, as in .gitignore an include, as the extend of ruff.toml, which reads an own file, a file that the installer writes whole under .agents/ units, such as the items of .pre-commit-config.yaml scripts/formats.json lists the shared files and the format of each. A package names its parts with the key parts. A profile and its tools have it in profile.json, and a role has it in install_extras.parts of skill-package.json. A role names a starter file, written once, with install_extras.starter. The key parts in .agents/stack.json records each part. just uninstall reads it to take the parts out again. Shared files and the record, in docs/stack-guide.md, tells how. If the project has no Justfile, the installer writes a starter Justfile. Otherwise it names the line to add to your Justfile. If the project has no pyproject.toml, package.json or Cargo.toml, the installer makes one with uv init --bare, npm init --yes or cargo init --vcs none. For Python, the profile also adds default-groups = "all" to pyproject.toml as a part, so that uv run has the tools. If a tool fails, a later just install tries it again. When the last package of a dependency group goes, the installer takes out the empty group.

title: jnterfaces
text: just install lint tasker turns on a tool and a role. just install tasker=gitwt turns on a role with a variant. just uninstall python takes out a profile with its tools, its recipes and its package. The project keeps pyproject.toml. just uninstall reporter lint turns them off. It removes the files of the role and the packages that just install added for the tool. It keeps each file that you edited, and each package that the project had before. If you remove a package by hand and add it back with no install between, it still counts as added. To keep it, take it out of owned_packages in .agents/stack.json. --profile python,typescript sets the profiles. A saved profile that the list leaves out is turned off. --defaults takes the defaults, and --all takes every role. --answer KEY=VALUE answers a setup question and saves the answer. The next section lists the questions. --ask asks again, even when the project has saved choices. --update first fast-forwards each package clone that the run uses. It does not change a clone with uncommitted changes, or a clone on another branch. The stack guide gives the rules. --clone NAME=DIR uses one clone in another folder. --clean installs the last commit of each clone, without uncommitted changes. --dry-run checks everything and writes nothing in the project. --check compares the record in .agents/stack.json with the shared files, and changes nothing.

title: jnterfaces
text: Some choices of a project belong to you, not to the stack. The installer asks each question that has no saved answer: Key Question Answers Default issues Which Gest tasks become GitHub issues? top, development, none top docs-publish Publish the docs site of a public repository after a merge to main? Only while the docs role is on. yes, no yes integration Run the integration tests in just check, or only in just verify before a PR? check, verify check tasker One branch in the main checkout, or a worktree for each task? Only while the tasker role is on. git, gitwt git review-model Which model does the adversarial review? strongest, or a model name strongest At a terminal, the installer asks each open question. Type the answer, its number, or nothing for the default. With no terminal, for example under an agent, the installer prints a SETUP_QUESTIONS v1 packet with the open questions, and stops. It writes nothing. The agent asks you each question, then runs just install again with --answer KEY=VALUE for each answer. With --defaults, or in CI, the installer takes the default of each open question and asks nothing. CI counts when the variable CI is set and is not 0 or false. A run that only removes, such as just uninstall reporter, asks nothing. A dry run takes the defaults and names the open questions. The answers are in the key answers of .agents/stack.json. A question with an answer is not asked again. A later version of the stack can add questions, and then only the new ones are asked. The answer integration=verify takes integration out of the steps of just check. The recipe stays, and just verify runs it once. The verify of the profile runs it when its tools list integration. Else the root verify has a line of its own for it. The answer of tasker is the variant of the role, as in just install tasker=gitwt.

title: jnterfaces
text: Each package is a Git clone in one folder. The default folder is ~/.local/share/skill-packages. Set SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR to use another folder, for example the folder of your own clones. If a clone is missing, the installer clones it from GitHub. JNTERFACES_DIR names one jnterfaces clone. Only jnterfaces has an installer. The other packages list their skills, and their other files, in skill-package.json. The installer copies them from the clone, and it writes one record for each package, such as .agents/nossaifd-install.json. A record holds the source revision and a hash of each file. The installer never overwrites or removes a file that you edited. It names the file and installs the rest. For each installed skill, it also makes the link .claude/skills/NAME for Claude Code. Before it writes, it checks every package. If one check fails, it writes nothing. A record from an older installer lists no skills and no hooks. The installer then reads the files of the old source revision in the clone. So it removes the old copies of skills and hooks that it shipped, and it keeps your edits. skill-package.json names the other files of a package in install_extras: files are files or folders outside .agents/skills, such as hook scripts. The installer manages them like the files of a skill. merge_hooks are JSON settings files. The installer adds their hooks entries to the file of the same name in the project, and it takes them out again on removal. seed maps a file of the project to a starter file. The installer writes it only when the project does not have it. The list of packages, roles, aliases and profiles is in stack.json. The stack guide builds a project in layers, from a project with no code to a project with lint and tests. It says what works now and what does not. The files of the stack gives each file that the installer reads or writes, each of its keys, and how the files work together.

title: jnterfaces
text: A recipe runs with sh, not with your shell. A git hook, a GUI program and CI do not read .zshrc. So a recipe must not need a setting from it. just env-lab runs just check with a clean environment, which keeps only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL and TERM. just env-lab test lint runs those recipes. A recipe with arguments goes in quotes, as in just env-lab "test -k name". PATH stays. The lab keeps the PATH of your shell, so a PATH that .zshrc sets is not tested. A GUI program may have a shorter PATH. A recipe that fails there runs again in your shell. When it passes in your shell, the lab names it. It also lists the variables of your shell that the recipe may need. They are the variables that the recipe, the recipes that it depends on, and the assignments of its module read. That list is a hint. It can miss a variable behind a dependency in another module (m::x), an alias, or an assignment without export. It never prints a value. It says to put the setting in the Justfile with set export, or in an ignored .env file with set dotenv-load. The lab runs a failed recipe twice, so use it on recipes that can run again.

title: jnterfaces
section: When the Justfile does not parse
text: just install is a recipe, so it cannot run when just cannot read the Justfile. This occurs, for example, when you remove a recipe that a recipe of the index uses, and just says Recipe `check` has unknown dependency `lint` . Run the installer itself in the folder of the project, the folder with .agents/install.just. It writes the index again for the recipes that the Justfile has now. In another folder, the command stops and writes nothing: jn_dir="${JNTERFACES_DIR:-${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces}" if [ ! -f .agents/install.just ]; then echo "Run this in the folder of the project, which has .agents/install.just" >&2; false elif [ -f "$jn_dir/scripts/install_stack.py" ] || git clone --quiet https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces "$jn_dir"; then uv run --script "$jn_dir/scripts/install_stack.py" --target . fi Then run just install --check. When a later edit breaks the Justfile, in docs/stack-guide.md, gives each cause.

title: jnterfaces
text: .agents/install.just defines the variable jn_copier, which runs copier 9 through uvx. copier makes files from a template, and copier update brings in a later version of the template. Any recipe of the project can use it, for example {{jn_copier}} copy TEMPLATE FOLDER.

title: jnterfaces
text: You can also install the skills with npx: npx skills add rahuldave/jnterfaces -a codex --skill just -y The npx route installs no tools and records no source revision in .agents/. The skills use these executables: just runs the recipes, and uv runs the installer and the tools. jagt renders and checks packets, from https://github.com/rahuldave/jagt. The skill needs jagt 0.3.0 or later, which gives each packet a nonce. Install the release binary with curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rahuldave/jagt/v0.6.4/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --tag v0.6.4. To build it from source instead, run cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/rahuldave/jagt --tag v0.6.4 jagt. cx runs incremental stages, from https://github.com/rahuldave/cx. Install the release binary with curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rahuldave/cx/v0.2.3/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --tag v0.2.3. To build it from source instead, run cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/rahuldave/cx --tag v0.2.3 cx.

title: jnterfaces
text: Each package works alone, and each skill works without the optional skills: just is the only required skill. cx and jagt-protocol are optional. Each fact has one source. The packet rules are in jagt-protocol, and the cx rules are in cx. The just skill points to them. A link to a skill that may be missing has a fallback in the same paragraph, for example “If the cx skill is not installed, …”. scripts/check_skill_links.py checks this rule, and just lint runs it. The other packages run it in their CI too.

title: jnterfaces
text: Command What it does just lint Checks the syntax of the scripts, the Python and the JSON, and the links between skills. just test Runs the tests of the installers, the link checker and the skills, in parallel with pytest. just test tests/test_skills.py runs one module. just install-into   [names] Runs the installer on another project. just check Runs just tools-check, just release-check, just lint, just package-lint and just test. Every commit must pass it. CI runs no recipe outside it. just package-lint clones from GitHub, so it needs the network. just release-check Prints the next tag. It needs no network. section: Lines that no test can run
text: Stable Rust has no comment that leaves one line out of the coverage. The steps read both lists from the parent commit. So a new entry counts only after it is in a commit of its own. Write the reason for each entry in a comment line, which starts with #, above it.

title: Start a Python, TypeScript or Rust project
section: What the stack does not give
text: Add these parts yourself: CI. No profile writes a GitHub Actions workflow. Without the tasker role, the prose role writes only one that checks the prose of a pull request. The check.yml of the tasker role runs no step of your languages until you add the step to the list ci of .agents/stack.json. Then add the setup that the step needs, as its comments say. A locked setup. just setup runs uv sync, not uv sync --locked. testpaths. pytest searches the whole project for tests. Set testpaths = ["tests"] under [tool.pytest.ini_options] to search one folder. title: The files of the stack
text: This page lists each file that the stack reads or writes, the meaning of each key in it, and how the files work together. How the stack fits together tells what an install does, and this page gives the files behind it. The examples come from an install into an empty Python project on 2026-10-31, with the command just install --profile python --defaults.

title: The files of the stack
text: Term Meaning package A Git repository that ships skills, for example nossaifd. clone The local Git clone of a package. The installer reads each package from its clone. role The name of a job, for example tasker. One package does the job. profile A language setup, for example python. A profile package, such as jnprofile-python, ships it. tool One unit of a profile, for example lint. It brings packages, recipes and parts. owner A thing that adds to the files of a project: jnterfaces, a profile, a tool, or a role. A tool has the key profile:tool, for example python:lint. shared file A file that more than one owner, and you, can add to, for example .gitignore or pyproject.toml. part What one owner adds to one shared file. unit The smallest piece of a part: one line, one key, one list item or one hook. record A JSON file in .agents/ that says what the installer wrote. own file A file that the installer writes whole under .agents/, for example .agents/config/python/ruff.toml or .agents/instructions/tasker.md. A shared file includes it or points to it.

title: The files of the stack
text: A project has one record of the stack, .agents/stack.json. A profile or a role does not bring a record of its own. Each run of the installer reads what the packages declare, and writes all of it into this one file. Two other names can confuse you: stack.json at the top of jnterfaces is the catalog. It lists the packages, roles and profiles. It is not in your project. .agents/ -install.json is one file for each package. It keeps the hashes of the skill files that the package copied in. It does not hold the shared files.

title: The files of the stack

File Where Who writes it What it holds stack.json jnterfaces the author of jnterfaces The catalog: each package, role and profile. scripts/formats.json jnterfaces the author of jnterfaces The format of each shared file that a part can go to. skill-package.json each package the author of the package The skills and the extras of the package. profile.json each profile package the author of the profile The tools of the profile, and the parts of each tool. .agents/stack.json the project the installer The record of the stack: your choices and each part. .agents/ -install.json the project the installer The record of one package: its revision and the hash of each of its files. .agents/stack-pending.json the project the installer The state of a run that has not finished. In a Justfile of your own, the installer adds one block with the line import? '.agents/install.just'.
